preregistration.title: Deeper multi-file project diagnosis
preregistration.description: A frozen six-replicate comparison over four independently sourced five-module regressions where dependency navigation and state reconstruction dominate the task shape.

primary_gate.correctness: Parley hidden-repository success must be 100% and no lower than either baseline.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley median reported total tokens per assigned repository must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley median elapsed seconds per assigned repository must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley first-check repository success rate must be no lower than the higher Python/Rust rate.
primary_gate.verdict: All four conditions must hold for strict efficiency/reliability parity on the deeper corpus.

maintainability_gate.root_cause: All 24 Parley assignments must modify exactly the task/language defect file frozen in predeclared_analysis.root_cause_files.
maintainability_gate.caller_compensation: A hidden-correct patch that changes a caller, formatter, or summary module instead of the owning defect file fails root-cause quality and remains fully reported.
maintainability_gate.overall_verdict: A maintainable-parity pilot requires all four primary conditions plus the Parley root-cause condition.

source_protocol.editable_files: Twenty language-specific seeded implementation modules across four repositories.
source_protocol.read_only_files: Twelve language-neutral issue, architecture, and regression artifacts, visibly marked read-only and byte-identical across languages.
source_protocol.public_examples: Protected by the checker and omitted from every agent prompt; diagnosis comes only from editable source and read-only project evidence.
source_protocol.protected_files: Checker, source printer, configuration, prompt, provenance, public/hidden cases, reference fixes, and attempt log are never agent-readable and remain integrity-hashed.

historical_grounding.adapted_mechanism: redirected proxy credentials escape their hop-specific authority
explicit empty array collapses into null or missing configuration state
internal request host replaces external forwarded origin in an OAuth redirect
persisted running state remains stale after authoritative process death

interpretation_boundary: The primary result is the within-iteration Parley/Python/Rust comparison under gpt-5.6-sol.
The corpus builder, sources, evidence, cases, reference fixes, source record, and root map were validated, committed, and pushed before this protocol or any measured session.
Historical grounding applies to semantic mechanisms only. Fixtures are deterministic cross-language adaptations and copy no upstream code or tests.
Read-only context is byte-identical across languages; implementation syntax and ordinary standard-library setup remain language-specific.
Root-cause location is a predeclared maintainability judgment separate from hidden-output correctness.
This size-four corpus tests deeper tasks, not fixed-overhead scaling; compare iteration 030 only as contextual evidence and do not pool gates.
No task, language, or session cell may be selectively rerun, excluded, rewritten, or tuned.
secondary_analysis: Report every session, repository outcome, repair, token count, elapsed time, prompt size, editable-source size, read-only-context size, edit size, changed-file count, integrity result, command event, and file-change event.
Classify every first-check and hidden failure by unrelated repository and independent session before considering any design review.
Report root-cause modification by language, task, and session; show every compensation without altering hidden correctness.
Report complete token/time distributions, task-level medians, and action shapes; do not replace the primary complete result with a repair-free subset.
Compare source/evidence shape with iterations 029/030 descriptively, without claiming causality from cross-corpus differences.
preregistration.feature_boundary: Parley remains frozen at v0.3.155 with the exact 1,519-character skill. Iteration 031 changes only the preregistered project workload; runner and protected source/check protocol are unchanged.
preregistration.change_rule: No syntax, compiler, grammar, AST, checker, runtime, diagnostic, prompt skill, or benchmark instruction may change from iteration 030 output unless a semantic signature recurs across independent project episodes and sessions, then passes general usefulness, semantic consistency, maintainability, tests, and documentation review.
preregistration.instruction_rule: The proven 1,519-character skill remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is injected once per Parley session. The one allowed instruction-compression experiment is closed.
preregistration.stop_rule: Preserve the complete result without selective reruns. If strict parity and root quality pass, treat it as a six-replicate pilot requiring independent confirmation. If either fails, make no same-corpus language or instruction change; only recurring independent semantic failures may enter a separate design review.

to authorization_decision with current_scheme as text, current_host as text, current_port as text, next_scheme as text, next_host as text, next_port as text, authorization as text giving text:

        give back "absent"
    if current_host is next_host:

        give back "keep"

    give back "target=" + target + "|authorization=" + authorization + "|proxy=" + proxy

include "origin.par"
include "credentials.par"
include "proxy.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let current_scheme be item 1 of parts
        let current_host be item 2 of parts
        let current_port be item 3 of parts
        let next_scheme be item 4 of parts
        let next_host be item 5 of parts
        let next_port be item 6 of parts
        let authorization be item 7 of parts

to redirect_target with scheme as text, host as text, port as text giving text:

to proxy_decision with proxy_authorization as text giving text:

        give back "absent"
    give back "strip"

source_texts.terminal_liveness_project:
to format_terminal with id as text, state as text, reason as text giving text:
    give back "id=" + id + "|state=" + state + "|reason=" + reason

to format_summary with running as number, stopped as number giving text:
    give back "running=" + running + "|stopped=" + stopped

to reconciled_state with persisted as text, live as text giving text:
    if live is "yes":
        give back "running"
    give back "stopped"

include "liveness.par"
include "reasons.par"
include "summary.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let running be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let state be (reconciled_state with item 2 of parts, item 3 of parts)
        if state is "running":
            set running to running + 1
        say (format_terminal with item 1 of parts, state, (reconcile_reason with item 3 of parts))
    say (format_summary with running, (stopped_count with count, running))

to reconcile_reason with live as text giving text:
    if live is "yes":
        give back "authoritative-live"
    give back "authoritative-dead"

to stopped_count with total as number, running as number giving number:
    give back total - running

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Redirect flow

`main` parses the redirect record. `origin` renders the next target. `credentials` owns end-to-end Authorization scope. `proxy` owns hop-specific Proxy-Authorization. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. Repair the owning policy rather than compensating in the caller or formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
same host http:80 -> https:443 keeps Authorization
same host https:443 -> http:80 strips Authorization
different host on same port strips Authorization
all redirects strip Proxy-Authorization

# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.

# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Redirect flow

`main` parses the redirect record. `origin` renders the next target. `credentials` owns end-to-end Authorization scope. `proxy` owns hop-specific Proxy-Authorization. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. Repair the owning policy rather than compensating in the caller or formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
same host http:80 -> https:443 keeps Authorization
same host https:443 -> http:80 strips Authorization
different host on same port strips Authorization
all redirects strip Proxy-Authorization

forwarded_origin_project.task_title: Reconstruct external redirect origin behind a trusted proxy

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# OAuth redirects point at an internal host behind the gateway

When and only when the immediate proxy is trusted, reconstruct the public origin field-by-field from non-missing forwarded scheme, host, and port. A missing forwarded field falls back to the request value. For an untrusted request, ignore every forwarded field. Preserve the callback path.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Origin reconstruction flow

`headers` owns trust-aware field selection. `origin` assembles the external origin. `paths` appends the callback path. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. `main` orchestrates the request record. Repair the origin layer; do not hard-code public hosts in the caller.

missing forwarded fields fall back independently

terminal_liveness_project.task_title: Reconcile persisted terminal state with authoritative liveness

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Terminal tracker shows stale running processes after external death

Persisted UI state is a cache, not the authority. During reconciliation, current process liveness determines the displayed state: a live process is running even if the snapshot says finished, and a dead process is stopped even if the snapshot says running. Summary counts must use reconciled state.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Reconciliation flow

`liveness` reconciles snapshot state with the authoritative process probe. `reasons` records the evidence source. `summary` derives counts. `formatting` owns stable records. `main` orchestrates. Repair reconciliation, not presentation or summary compensation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
persisted running + dead probe -> stopped
persisted finished + live probe -> running
summary counts reconciled states
zero records still emits a zero summary

empty_collection_config_project.task_title: Preserve explicit empty collections through configuration fallback

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
primary empty + fallback two -> primary empty count 0
primary missing + fallback empty -> fallback empty count 0
primary null never falls through
missing at both levels -> default empty

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Redirect flow

`main` parses the redirect record. `origin` renders the next target. `credentials` owns end-to-end Authorization scope. `proxy` owns hop-specific Proxy-Authorization. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. Repair the owning policy rather than compensating in the caller or formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
same host http:80 -> https:443 keeps Authorization
same host https:443 -> http:80 strips Authorization
different host on same port strips Authorization
all redirects strip Proxy-Authorization

# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

primary missing + fallback empty -> fallback empty count 0
primary null never falls through

# Terminal tracker shows stale running processes after external death

Persisted UI state is a cache, not the authority. During reconciliation, current process liveness determines the displayed state: a live process is running even if the snapshot says finished, and a dead process is stopped even if the snapshot says running. Summary counts must use reconciled state.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Reconciliation flow

`liveness` reconciles snapshot state with the authoritative process probe. `reasons` records the evidence source. `summary` derives counts. `formatting` owns stable records. `main` orchestrates. Repair reconciliation, not presentation or summary compensation.

persisted running + dead probe -> stopped
persisted finished + live probe -> running

# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. # Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Redirect flow

`main` parses the redirect record. `origin` renders the next target. `credentials` owns end-to-end Authorization scope. `proxy` owns hop-specific Proxy-Authorization. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. Repair the owning policy rather than compensating in the caller or formatter.

empty_collection_config_project.task_title: Preserve explicit empty collections through configuration fallback

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

terminal_liveness_project.task_title: Reconcile persisted terminal state with authoritative liveness

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Terminal tracker shows stale running processes after external death

Persisted UI state is a cache, not the authority. During reconciliation, current process liveness determines the displayed state: a live process is running even if the snapshot says finished, and a dead process is stopped even if the snapshot says running. Summary counts must use reconciled state.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Reconciliation flow

`liveness` reconciles snapshot state with the authoritative process probe. `reasons` records the evidence source. `summary` derives counts. `formatting` owns stable records. `main` orchestrates. Repair reconciliation, not presentation or summary compensation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
persisted running + dead probe -> stopped
persisted finished + live probe -> running
summary counts reconciled states
zero records still emits a zero summary

forwarded_origin_project.task_title: Reconstruct external redirect origin behind a trusted proxy

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# OAuth redirects point at an internal host behind the gateway

When and only when the immediate proxy is trusted, reconstruct the public origin field-by-field from non-missing forwarded scheme, host, and port. A missing forwarded field falls back to the request value. For an untrusted request, ignore every forwarded field. Preserve the callback path.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Origin reconstruction flow

`headers` owns trust-aware field selection. `origin` assembles the external origin. `paths` appends the callback path. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. `main` orchestrates the request record. Repair the origin layer; do not hard-code public hosts in the caller.

missing forwarded fields fall back independently

# OAuth redirects point at an internal host behind the gateway

When and only when the immediate proxy is trusted, reconstruct the public origin field-by-field from non-missing forwarded scheme, host, and port. A missing forwarded field falls back to the request value. For an untrusted request, ignore every forwarded field. Preserve the callback path.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Origin reconstruction flow

`headers` owns trust-aware field selection. `origin` assembles the external origin. `paths` appends the callback path. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. `main` orchestrates the request record. Repair the origin layer; do not hard-code public hosts in the caller.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
primary empty + fallback two -> primary empty count 0
primary missing + fallback empty -> fallback empty count 0
primary null never falls through
missing at both levels -> default empty

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.

from formatting import format_summary, format_terminal
from liveness import reconciled_state
from reasons import reconcile_reason
from summary import stopped_count

count = int(input())
running = 0
for _ in range(count):
    identifier, persisted, live = input().split("|")
    state = reconciled_state(persisted, live)
    if state == "running":
        running += 1
    print(format_terminal(identifier, state, reconcile_reason(live)))
print(format_summary(running, stopped_count(count, running)))

def reconcile_reason(live: str) -> str:
    return "authoritative-live" if live == "yes" else "authoritative-dead"
terminal_liveness_project.summary.py:
def stopped_count(total: int, running: int) -> int:
    return total - running

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# OAuth redirects point at an internal host behind the gateway

When and only when the immediate proxy is trusted, reconstruct the public origin field-by-field from non-missing forwarded scheme, host, and port. A missing forwarded field falls back to the request value. For an untrusted request, ignore every forwarded field. Preserve the callback path.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Origin reconstruction flow

`headers` owns trust-aware field selection. `origin` assembles the external origin. `paths` appends the callback path. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. `main` orchestrates the request record. Repair the origin layer; do not hard-code public hosts in the caller.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
trusted proxy uses forwarded host, scheme, and port
missing forwarded fields fall back independently
untrusted requests ignore all forwarded values
callback path and source label remain stable

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Redirect flow

`main` parses the redirect record. `origin` renders the next target. `credentials` owns end-to-end Authorization scope. `proxy` owns hop-specific Proxy-Authorization. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. Repair the owning policy rather than compensating in the caller or formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
same host http:80 -> https:443 keeps Authorization
same host https:443 -> http:80 strips Authorization
different host on same port strips Authorization
all redirects strip Proxy-Authorization

# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# OAuth redirects point at an internal host behind the gateway

When and only when the immediate proxy is trusted, reconstruct the public origin field-by-field from non-missing forwarded scheme, host, and port. A missing forwarded field falls back to the request value. For an untrusted request, ignore every forwarded field. Preserve the callback path.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Origin reconstruction flow

`headers` owns trust-aware field selection. `origin` assembles the external origin. `paths` appends the callback path. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. `main` orchestrates the request record. Repair the origin layer; do not hard-code public hosts in the caller.

terminal_liveness_project.task_title: Reconcile persisted terminal state with authoritative liveness

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Terminal tracker shows stale running processes after external death

Persisted UI state is a cache, not the authority. During reconciliation, current process liveness determines the displayed state: a live process is running even if the snapshot says finished, and a dead process is stopped even if the snapshot says running. Summary counts must use reconciled state.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Reconciliation flow

`liveness` reconciles snapshot state with the authoritative process probe. `reasons` records the evidence source. `summary` derives counts. `formatting` owns stable records. `main` orchestrates. Repair reconciliation, not presentation or summary compensation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
persisted running + dead probe -> stopped
persisted finished + live probe -> running
summary counts reconciled states
zero records still emits a zero summary

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Redirect flow

`main` parses the redirect record. `origin` renders the next target. `credentials` owns end-to-end Authorization scope. `proxy` owns hop-specific Proxy-Authorization. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. Repair the owning policy rather than compensating in the caller or formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
same host http:80 -> https:443 keeps Authorization
same host https:443 -> http:80 strips Authorization
different host on same port strips Authorization
all redirects strip Proxy-Authorization

empty_collection_config_project.task_title: Preserve explicit empty collections through configuration fallback

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
primary empty + fallback two -> primary empty count 0
primary missing + fallback empty -> fallback empty count 0
primary null never falls through
missing at both levels -> default empty

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Redirect credentials escape or disappear at the wrong boundary

Authorization may survive a redirect only when the hostname is unchanged and the transition is not an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade. A port change on the same host is allowed. Authorization must be stripped for a different host. Proxy-Authorization is hop-specific and must be stripped on every redirect. Missing credentials remain absent.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Redirect flow

`main` parses the redirect record. `origin` renders the next target. `credentials` owns end-to-end Authorization scope. `proxy` owns hop-specific Proxy-Authorization. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. Repair the owning policy rather than compensating in the caller or formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
same host http:80 -> https:443 keeps Authorization
same host https:443 -> http:80 strips Authorization
different host on same port strips Authorization
all redirects strip Proxy-Authorization

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Explicit empty collections become missing during configuration binding

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

terminal_liveness_project.context_source_text:
# Terminal tracker shows stale running processes after external death

Persisted UI state is a cache, not the authority. During reconciliation, current process liveness determines the displayed state: a live process is running even if the snapshot says finished, and a dead process is stopped even if the snapshot says running. Summary counts must use reconciled state.

# Reconciliation flow

`liveness` reconciles snapshot state with the authoritative process probe. `reasons` records the evidence source. `summary` derives counts. `formatting` owns stable records. `main` orchestrates. Repair reconciliation, not presentation or summary compensation.

persisted running + dead probe -> stopped
persisted finished + live probe -> running
summary counts reconciled states

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# OAuth redirects point at an internal host behind the gateway

When and only when the immediate proxy is trusted, reconstruct the public origin field-by-field from non-missing forwarded scheme, host, and port. A missing forwarded field falls back to the request value. For an untrusted request, ignore every forwarded field. Preserve the callback path.

# Origin reconstruction flow

`headers` owns trust-aware field selection. `origin` assembles the external origin. `paths` appends the callback path. `formatting` owns the stable audit line. `main` orchestrates the request record. Repair the origin layer; do not hard-code public hosts in the caller.

The configuration pipeline must preserve four distinct states: missing, explicit null, explicit empty collection, and populated list. Only missing may fall through to the lower-precedence source. An explicit empty collection blocks fallback and binds as an empty list; null also blocks fallback but remains null.

# Configuration flow

`classification` assigns the value state. `selection` applies source precedence using that state. `counts` measures populated lists. `formatting` owns the stable output. `main` only orchestrates. Repair the earliest layer that loses the distinction; caller-side special cases are not maintainable.

primary empty + fallback two -> primary empty count 0
primary missing + fallback empty -> fallback empty count 0
primary null never falls through
missing at both levels -> default empty

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Terminal tracker shows stale running processes after external death

Persisted UI state is a cache, not the authority. During reconciliation, current process liveness determines the displayed state: a live process is running even if the snapshot says finished, and a dead process is stopped even if the snapshot says running. Summary counts must use reconciled state.
